narrative.title: Sorting the Bay by Signal Class
narrative.scenario: A warehouse chain lists pallets each carrying one of three signal classes — 0, 1, or 2 — and the floor plan demands all 0-class pallets up front, 2-class at the far end, 1-class in between. Because only three classes exist, a tally pass followed by an overwrite pass re-stamps the chain in class order without building anything new.
narrative.inputFormat: An array head of node values, each of which is 0, 1, or 2.
narrative.outputFormat: The values after segregation: all 0s first, then all 1s, then all 2s.

testCases.explanation: One zero, two ones, five twos — the rewrite lays them out in class order.
No 1-class pallets exist; the zero leads and the twos follow.

hintLevels: Level 1: With only three possible values you do not need a general sort — you need three counters.
Level 2: Tally the counts of 0, 1, and 2 in one pass, then walk the chain again writing 0s, then 1s, then 2s over the node values.
Level 3: The overwrite trick works because node identity is irrelevant here — only the multiset of values matters; relinking three sub-lists is the alternative when values must not be mutated.
